transcript: Last week, Paul and I went to see prayer for the French Republic on Broadway produced by Manhattan Theatre Club. This is an extremely timely play. It's kind of a big meditation on antisemitism, activism, and accountability. But do not let that heavy subject matter intimidate you because the play is also just a phenomenal family story and it's really quite comedic a lot of the time too — it was like way funnier than I expected. And even though the writing in the play is so smart and dense and interesting and layered, I totally felt invited to engage in these intellectual and political conversations as someone who's both not Jewish and definitely no expert on any of the themes discussed. I thought this piece did a great job of striking a balance between having something to express and not alienating or just feeding non -contextualized rhetoric to the audience. At its core it's a strong story and a strong piece of theater too. With that, another playbill for my collection.
